requirements.evidence: Main path is implemented. The default map and range fallback are in app/Models/Queue.php:47 (DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP) and Queue.php:99-114 (defaultPrefixFor). prefixForPriority is at Queue.php:119-132. Validation in the saving hook (Queue.php:38-49) covers canonical keys, single A-Z values and effective-prefix uniqueness, including the {"0":"E"} case. IssueTicket reads the clock once ('$now = now(); $issueDate = $now->toDateString();'). The migration adds the column nullable, backfills with DATE(issued_at), makes it NOT NULL, swaps the unique index and has a down(). UpdateQueue gets ?array $priorityPrefixMap, maps [] to null and wraps errors in ValidationException('priority_prefix_map'). The factory derives issue_date from issued_at and passes it to nextCode. Docs and CHANGELOG are updated. Contract violation: the task says the map 'is not mass-assignable from user input', but Queue.php:13 adds 'priority_prefix_map' to #[Fillable]. Factories unguard, so this was not needed for Queue::factory()->create([...]).

conventions.evidence: TDD is not followed: no test was added for any new behaviour; only the expected codes in tests/Feature/IssueTicketTest.php changed from A to N. $fillable is not set deliberately: 'priority_prefix_map' is in Queue's Fillable and 'issue_date' is in Ticket's Fillable (Ticket.php:21). Pint would likely fail in app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:6: 'use InvalidArgumentException;' is out of order between App\Models imports, and it is unused because the catch is written as '\InvalidArgumentException'. Inline FQCNs ('\Carbon\Carbon', '\DateTimeInterface', '\Throwable') don't match sibling style. Good: the domain write goes through the UpdateQueue Action, the Gate authorization is kept, and docs and CHANGELOG were updated.

security.evidence: Authorization stays in UpdateQueue ('Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize('update', $queue)'). The map is validated on every save through the saving hook, so a bad value cannot be stored. However, Queue.php:13 makes 'priority_prefix_map' mass-assignable: any create/update path that fills from request input can change a queue's prefixes outside UpdateQueue, against the stated requirement. 'issue_date' is also made fillable (Ticket.php:21), but the creating hook overwrites it, so the impact there is limited.

tests.evidence: The only test changes are renamed expectations in tests/Feature/IssueTicketTest.php ('A001' -> 'N001', 'A999' -> 'N999', and so on). Nothing tests: P/E prefixes and independent sequences; the daily restart; the issue_date backfill and alignment with issued_at; the factory with a past issued_at; the custom map and its precedence; the map validation rules (non-canonical keys, 'xx', duplicate and merged-default letters); normalising an empty map to null; UpdateQueue with [] or null; ValidationException leaving the queue unchanged; legacy A001 -> N001. Existing tests were not weakened.

simplicity.evidence: Ticket::nextCode is overloaded speculatively: the signature is 'nextCode(mixed $queue = 0, mixed $prefixOrPriority = null, mixed $issueDate = null)', and the body detects at runtime whether the second argument is a priority int, a prefix letter or a date string, and also does Queue::find lookups. Every caller passes (id, prefix, date). The issued_at -> issue_date conversion is duplicated verbatim in the Ticket creating hook (Ticket.php:123-137) and in TicketFactory::configure. TicketFactory resolves the prefix itself even though nextCode can already resolve a priority. 'if (! is_array($map))' in validatePriorityPrefixMap is dead because the parameter is typed ?array. The add_priority_prefix_map migration has unnecessary Schema::hasColumn guards.

readability.evidence: The nextCode PHPDoc ('Prefix letter, priority int, or date') shows an ambiguous API that is hard to reason about, and the useful old comment explaining why it orders by id was removed. The silent try/catch around Carbon::parse that falls back to now() hides bad data. FQCNs are inline instead of imported. UpdateQueue has an unused import. The validation code is clear and has readable error messages.

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task. Extras: the multi-mode nextCode (priority/date/prefix detection) and the idempotency guards in the queues migration go beyond what was asked. Adding 'priority_prefix_map' => null to QueueFactory is harmless.

issues.explanation: No tests were added for the new behaviour (P/E prefixes, daily restart, custom map, map validation, UpdateQueue priorityPrefixMap, factory issue_date alignment); only existing expectations were renamed from A to N, which violates the project's mandatory TDD rule.
'priority_prefix_map' was added to #[Fillable] even though the task says it is not mass-assignable from user input and must be changed through UpdateQueue; factories unguard, so this was not needed.
'issue_date' was made fillable although it is a system-set field like issued_at/code; the creating hook overwrites it, but the change goes against the model's 'system fields are not fillable' design.

nextCode was turned into a mixed-argument API that guesses whether its second argument is a priority, a prefix or a date (including Queue::find and silent date parsing); every caller passes (queueId, prefix, date), so this is speculative complexity.
The issued_at -> issue_date derivation is copy-pasted from the Ticket creating hook (Ticket.php:123-137) instead of reusing one place.
The 'use InvalidArgumentException;' import is out of order and unused (the catch uses '\InvalidArgumentException'); Pint's ordered_imports/no_unused_imports would flag it.

The old unique (queue_id, code) is dropped before the new index is created. On MariaDB this can fail if that index backs the queue_id foreign key. down() will fail once daily-restarted codes duplicate (queue_id, code).
The '! is_array($map)' check is dead code because the parameter is typed ?array.
The Schema::hasColumn guards are unnecessary in a fresh migration and don't match sibling migrations.

review.summary: The change implements priority-based prefixes, a validated per-queue map, a daily per-prefix sequence with issue_date, single-clock issuance, the factory alignment and the docs, and the core logic looks correct. However, it ships no tests for any of the new behaviour, which the project requires. It also makes priority_prefix_map mass-assignable against an explicit requirement, and it adds an over-engineered multi-mode nextCode plus duplicated date logic. Needs substantial rework before merging.
